messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT • runtime.canary - latency regression detected • severity: P2 • link: https://infra.redwood/alerts/1767070707 :rotating_light:

morgan.sre: ack, paging in. joining the channel. looking at canary cluster canary-7

dave.runtime: i'm on it too. rolled the adaptive-batching heuristic last night (~22:10 UTC). did we path traffic to canary-7 for the release? @leah.prod-eng

leah.prod-eng: yes, canary weight bumped to 10% at 10:12 UTC per rollout dashboard https://rollouts.redwood/releases/2026-03-17/alpha

morgan.sre: metrics: p99 for /v1/generate spiked x3, error rate small but tail latency and CPU kernel fallbacks on gpu hosts

morgan.sre: logs (snippet):
```
2026-03-17T10:13:01Z kernel_select: preferred=quant_gpu, fallback=quant_kernel_cpu
2026-03-17T10:13:02Z batching_window_ms=1200 -> dropped to 64 after eviction
2026-03-17T10:13:03Z inference_timeout=8000ms
```

dave.runtime: that matches the batching heuristic mis-estimating sequence lengths -> large microbatches + kernel selector fallback. propose immediate mitigation: flip feature flag adaptive-batching.off and reduce canary weight to 0

morgan.sre: i can flip the flag now and scale canary to 0.5% while we validate. running:
```
$ curl -X POST https://flags.redwood/api/toggle -d '{"flag":"adaptive-batching","state":"off"}'
$ rolloutctl set-weight --env=prod --target=canary-7 --weight=0.5
```

infra-bot: ACTION: feature flag "adaptive-batching" toggled to OFF by morgan.sre at 1767070752

morgan.sre: done. canary traffic dropped to 0.5%, reducing new sessions to canary-7

leah.prod-eng: seeing immediate reduction in kernel fallback events on the canary hosts

sam.support: any customer-facing errors? are we seeing 5xx or timeouts surfaced to users?

morgan.sre: no large spike in 5xxs, but multiple downstream services report timeouts >10s for a subset of requests. pulling list of affected customer IDs now

pm-ken: please prepare a short status update for customers on the alpha cohort if we confirm impact. cc: security@redwood

dave.runtime: extra detail from runtime logs: kernel_selector.cpp prints
```
[WARN] kernel_selector: fallback_reason=exec_timeout threshold=1000ms observed=1200ms
[DEBUG] batch_manager: window_ms=1200 batch_size=48
```
Looks like the kernel selector timed out waiting for a batch, then fell back to CPU path with slower quant kernels.

morgan.sre: plan: keep ff off, keep canary at 0.5% for 10m to observe. if stable, proceed to rollback canary binary to v1.6.2 (pre-heuristic) and roll forward with controlled weight. i'll start rollback now.

infra-bot: ROLLBACK: canary-7 model binary -> v1.6.2 initiated by morgan.sre at 1767070815

leah.prod-eng: i'll take over monitoring once rollback completes. oncall handoff scheduled in 20m. saving traces and perf dumps to /var/logs/incidents/1767070707/

infra-bot: ROLLBACK COMPLETE • canary-7 now running v1.6.2 • traffic weight 0.5% • 1767070868

morgan.sre: metrics update: p99 has dropped back close to baseline within 90s of rollback. tail latencies normalized. linking graphs: https://graphs.redwood/1767070707/latency

sam.support: notifying alpha customers and CS leads now :phone: • message template shared in #ops-comm

pm-ken: good containment. please open INC ticket and assign owners for postmortem. include timeline, root cause hypothesis (batching heuristic + kernel selector race), and mitigation steps (ff kill + rollback)

morgan.sre: created INC-2026-078 at https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-078 • assignees: morgan.sre, dave.runtime • sev:P2 • impact: increased latency for small subset of alpha users, no widespread 5xx

dave.runtime: i'll dig into kernel selector timeout path and add extra guards to avoid blocking the fast path. will file a follow-up RFC for batching heuristic safety limits

leah.prod-eng: taking oncall handoff at 1767071520. leaving notes and recorded actions in the ticket. ping me if anything regresses.

morgan.sre: thanks all. incident => contained. moving to post-incident review and follow-up actions.
